title: Introduction to structs, members, and member selection
recap: A struct groups related members into one object. Member selection with the dot operator accesses a named part of that object.
Domain invariants still matter after grouping data. Equal dimensions alone do not make a valid square when the contract excludes zero and negative lengths.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice introduction to structs, members, and member selection.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement area(rectangle) and isSquare(rectangle). A rectangle with either dimension <= 0 is invalid: its area is 0 and isSquare is false. Otherwise area is width*height and a square has equal dimensions. Dimensions and products fit int.
hints: Access width and height through the parameter.
Square classification needs validity as well as equality.
